  "files": {
    "Dockerfile": "# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1\n\n# Headless RouteKitEval intern image. Two stages:\n#   1. routekit-eval-cli — fetches the standalone `routekit-eval` release binary (needs curl + CA certs)\n#   2. runtime — Bun + your workspace + the CLI in a user-writable dir (so\n#      `routekit-eval start --auto-update` can replace it) plus bash/curl for the updater\n#\n# `routekit-eval init --with-docker` writes this file into your workspace's deploy/ folder.\n#\n# Build from a workspace that contains `features/` (build context = workspace root):\n#   docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile -t routekit-eval .\n#\n# Run (inject the key; persist durable state in a named volume). tini is baked in\n# as PID 1, so `docker run --init` is optional:\n#   docker run --rm -p 7070:7070 \\\n#     -e ROUTEKIT_EVAL_BEARER_TOKEN=sk-or-... \\\n#     -v routekit-eval-state:/workspace/state routekit-eval\n#\n# IMPORTANT: add a `.dockerignore` at the workspace root so host-only files and\n# secrets are never baked in. Keeping `.routekit-eval/sdk` lets the build skip a\n# regeneration step, but it is optional — the build runs `routekit-eval init` to recreate\n# the SDK cache when the context lacks it (e.g. a fresh clone). Always drop:\n#   .git/\n#   node_modules/\n#   .routekit-eval/logs/\n#   .routekit-eval/state.sqlite*\n#   .routekit-eval/credentials.json\n#   .routekit-eval/start.json\n#\n# Runs on any linux/amd64 or linux/arm64 host. Managed container platforms\n# (Cloudflare Containers, E2B, Daytona, Runloop) require linux/amd64 — build with\n# `--platform linux/amd64`. See `routekit-eval start --help` for the runtime surface.\n\n# --- Stage 1: download the standalone routekit-eval CLI --------------------------------\nFROM debian:bookworm-slim AS routekit-eval-cli\nRUN apt-get update \\\n  && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates \\\n  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*\n# Installs a self-contained `routekit-eval` executable. Bun is NOT required to run the CLI\n# itself — only to run your workspace, which the runtime stage provides. The\n# installer fetches the latest published CLI; pin a version by pre-seeding the\n# binary instead if you need reproducible builds.\n# `export` so the `bash` on the receiving end of the pipe inherits ROUTEKIT_EVAL_INSTALL_DIR\n# — a bare `VAR=val curl ... | bash` prefix only scopes the var to `curl`, not to\n# the piped shell that actually runs the installer, so the binary would land in the\n# default location and the `/usr/local/bin/routekit-eval` check below would fail.\nRUN export ROUTEKIT_EVAL_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local/bin \\\n  && curl -fsSL --proto '=https' the RouteKit installation | bash \\\n  && /usr/local/bin/routekit-eval --version\n\n# --- Stage 2: runtime --------------------------------------------------------\nFROM oven/bun:1.3-slim AS runtime\n\n# tini as PID 1 forwards SIGTERM/SIGINT to `routekit-eval` and reaps exited child processes,\n# even on platforms that cannot pass `docker run --init` (e.g. Cloudflare\n# Containers). Layering `--init` on top of this is harmless. bash + curl + CA certs\n# are here for `routekit-eval start --auto-update`, which shells out to the public install\n# script to atomically swap the binary in place; drop them if you never auto-update.\nUSER root\nRUN apt-get update \\\n  && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends tini bash ca-certificates curl \\\n  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*\n\n# `routekit-eval start` listens here. 0.0.0.0 makes the port reachable from outside the\n# container; container network isolation is your security boundary. Do NOT publish\n# this port on an untrusted network without an authenticating reverse proxy — the\n# local runtime is unauthenticated. Override ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT to match a platform that\n# injects its own port.\nENV ROUTEKIT_EVAL_HOST=0.0.0.0 \\\n    ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT=7070 \\\n    # Keep the durable SQLite store OUT of .routekit-eval/ so a persistence volume never\n    # shadows the build-time SDK cache at .routekit-eval/sdk. A rebuild updates .routekit-eval/sdk in\n    # the image layer, but Docker never re-copies image content into an existing\n    # named volume — mounting over .routekit-eval/ would pin containers to a stale SDK.\n    ROUTEKIT_EVAL_STATE_DIR=/workspace/state\n\n# Install the CLI into a user-writable dir on PATH, alongside its `routekit-eval.version`\n# sidecar. Both are required for `routekit-eval start --auto-update`: the updater shells out\n# to the install script, which needs to write `routekit-eval`+`routekit-eval.version` into the binary's\n# own directory. A root-owned /usr/local/bin would be unwritable by the non-root\n# runtime user, and /home/bun keeps the binary out of /workspace so a mounted state\n# volume never shadows it. Auto-update stays OFF by default (opt in with\n# `--auto-update <level>` or `ROUTEKIT_EVAL_AUTO_UPDATE`); see the runbook for restart caveats.\nCOPY --from=routekit-eval-cli --chown=bun:bun /usr/local/bin/routekit-eval /home/bun/.local/bin/routekit-eval\nCOPY --from=routekit-eval-cli --chown=bun:bun /usr/local/bin/routekit-eval.version /home/bun/.local/bin/routekit-eval.version\nENV PATH=/home/bun/.local/bin:$PATH\n\n# Run everything as the image's unprivileged `bun` user so the build-time install\n# and runtime writes (SQLite, logs) never need root — otherwise a root-owned\n# `node_modules` blocks the non-root runtime.\nWORKDIR /workspace\nRUN chown bun:bun /workspace\nUSER bun\n\n# Copy the whole workspace, then install. We deliberately do NOT copy manifests\n# first for layer caching: the workspace's `routekit-eval` dependency is `file:.routekit-eval/sdk`, so\n# the local SDK package must already be on disk for `bun install` to resolve it.\n# Copying everything up front keeps this correct for both source checkouts and\n# `routekit-eval pack` bundles; the .dockerignore keeps `.routekit-eval/sdk` while dropping secrets.\nCOPY --chown=bun:bun . .\n\n# Materialize the workspace SDK cache when the build context lacks it — a fresh\n# `git clone` or a remote/CI builder will not carry gitignored `.routekit-eval/sdk`. `routekit-eval\n# init` regenerates it from the CLI's embedded copy with no network, and is a\n# no-op on contexts that already ship it (a laptop deploy or an `routekit-eval pack` bundle).\nRUN [ -d .routekit-eval/sdk ] || routekit-eval init . --no-install\nRUN bun install --frozen-lockfile || bun install\n\n# Durable state (the SQLite store: schedule history + feature state) lives in\n# ROUTEKIT_EVAL_STATE_DIR, a dedicated directory OUTSIDE `.routekit-eval/` so a persistence volume\n# never covers the build-time SDK cache at `.routekit-eval/sdk`. Mount a volume here to keep\n# state across restarts. NDJSON logs still land under `.routekit-eval/logs` on the ephemeral\n# image layer (the log path is not relocatable); bind-mount that path too if you\n# need to retain them. Platforms with ephemeral disks (e.g. Cloudflare Containers)\n# will not retain either.\nRUN mkdir -p \"$ROUTEKIT_EVAL_STATE_DIR\" /workspace/.routekit-eval\nVOLUME [\"/workspace/state\"]\n\n# Anchor HOME to the workspace so the harness runtime and skill caches that\n# resolve under `$HOME/.routekit-eval` (`~/.routekit-eval/pi-runtime`, `~/.routekit-eval/skills-cache`) land in\n# the writable workspace tree instead of the base image's /home/bun. Set after the\n# build steps so `bun install` keeps using the default cache location.\nENV HOME=/workspace\n\nEXPOSE 7070\n\n# /health returns 200 while the daemon is serving. Uses Bun (already present)\n# so the image needs no extra curl/wget. Managed platforms often ignore Docker\n# HEALTHCHECK and probe /health over HTTP themselves — this covers plain Docker.\nHEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=20s --retries=3 \\\n  CMD bun -e \"fetch('http://127.0.0.1:'+(process.env.ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT||7070)+'/health').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))\"\n\n# tini (ENTRYPOINT) is PID 1 and forwards signals to `routekit-eval`; the JSON CMD keeps a\n# shell only to expand $ROUTEKIT_EVAL_HOST/$ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT, then `exec`s so `routekit-eval` replaces it and\n# receives SIGTERM directly for a clean shutdown. `--global-auth` lets the injected\n# ROUTEKIT_EVAL_BEARER_TOKEN satisfy the credential gate; `--no-install` because deps are\n# baked in above, keeping boot fast.\n#\n# To auto-update in place, append `--auto-update patch --auto-update-restart exit`\n# and run the container with a restart policy (e.g. `docker run --restart\n# unless-stopped`, no `--rm`). The `exit` mode lets Docker relaunch the container\n# so it picks up the swapped binary from the writable layer; the default `reexec`\n# mode would double-spawn under tini and tear the container down.\nENTRYPOINT [\"tini\", \"--\"]\nCMD [\"sh\", \"-c\", \"exec routekit-eval start --global-auth --no-install --host \\\"$ROUTEKIT_EVAL_HOST\\\" --port \\\"$ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT\\\"\"]\n",
    "compose.yaml": "# Run the headless RouteKitEval intern locally with Docker or OrbStack in one command.\n#\n# `routekit-eval init --with-docker` writes this file (and the Dockerfile) into a deploy/ folder\n# in your workspace — the directory that contains features/. From the workspace root:\n#\n#   ROUTEKIT_EVAL_BEARER_TOKEN=sk-or-... docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml up --build\n#\n# Probe http://127.0.0.1:7070/health to confirm it is serving. Stop with Ctrl+C\n# (the SIGTERM drains the session); `docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml down -v`\n# also removes the state volume. OrbStack and Docker Desktop read this identically.\nname: routekit-eval\nservices:\n  routekit-eval:\n    build:\n      # Build context is the workspace root (parent of deploy/) so the image can\n      # copy features/ and .routekit-eval/sdk; the Dockerfile lives under deploy/.\n      context: ..\n      dockerfile: deploy/Dockerfile\n    environment:\n      # Fail fast with a clear message instead of a mystery credential error.\n      ROUTEKIT_EVAL_BEARER_TOKEN: ${ROUTEKIT_EVAL_BEARER_TOKEN:?export ROUTEKIT_EVAL_BEARER_TOKEN or add it to a .env file}\n      ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT: ${ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT:-7070}\n    ports:\n      - \"${ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT:-7070}:${ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT:-7070}\"\n    volumes:\n      # Durable SQLite state; matches ROUTEKIT_EVAL_STATE_DIR in the image. Drop this line to\n      # run fully stateless. `down -v` clears it.\n      - routekit-eval-state:/workspace/state\n    # Resource backstop: cap memory, swap, and process count so a leaked\n    # subprocess tree or main-process leak self-limits instead of thrashing the\n    # host. Docker cannot express percentage caps, so override the absolute\n    # defaults from the environment\n    # to match your machine (e.g. ROUTEKIT_EVAL_MEMORY_MAX=4g ROUTEKIT_EVAL_TASKS_MAX=256).\n    mem_limit: ${ROUTEKIT_EVAL_MEMORY_MAX:-10g}\n    # Disable container swap so a memory leak is promptly OOM-killed and restarted.\n    memswap_limit: ${ROUTEKIT_EVAL_MEMORY_MAX:-10g}\n    mem_reservation: ${ROUTEKIT_EVAL_MEMORY_HIGH:-8g}\n    pids_limit: ${ROUTEKIT_EVAL_TASKS_MAX:-512}\n    # unless-stopped survives daemon restarts and is the policy --auto-update needs\n    # (Docker relaunches the container so it picks up a swapped binary). It does not\n    # fight a manual Ctrl+C or `compose down`.\n    restart: unless-stopped\n    # tini (PID 1 in the image) forwards this SIGTERM; give the session time to drain.\n    stop_grace_period: 45s\nvolumes:\n  routekit-eval-state:\n",
    "routekit-eval-managed.conf": "[Service]\nMemoryHigh=53%\nMemoryMax=66%\nMemorySwapMax=0\nTasksMax=512\nRestart=always\nRestartSec=2\nKillSignal=SIGTERM\nKillMode=mixed\nTimeoutStopSec=45\n",
    "routekit-eval.service": "# systemd unit for a headless Gateway Intern (`routekit-eval start`).\n#\n# `routekit-eval init --with-systemd` writes this file into your workspace's deploy/ folder.\n#\n# Descriptive FHS layout:\n#   /var/lib/routekit-eval/.local/bin/routekit-eval   the CLI binary (service-owned + writable so\n#                                 `--auto-update` can replace it in place)\n#   /var/lib/routekit-eval                  the workspace + runtime state (features/, .routekit-eval/)\n#   /etc/routekit-eval/env                  secrets + tuning, root-owned and hidden from\n#                                 the service\n#\n# Install:\n#   1. Create a dedicated unprivileged user whose home is the workspace, then put\n#      your workspace (the directory containing `features/`) there:\n#        sudo useradd --system --home-dir /var/lib/routekit-eval --shell /usr/sbin/nologin routekit-eval\n#        sudo install -d -o routekit-eval -g routekit-eval /var/lib/routekit-eval\n#        # copy your workspace in, then: sudo chown -R routekit-eval:routekit-eval /var/lib/routekit-eval\n#   2. Store the secret + any tuning in /etc/routekit-eval/env. Keep it root-owned and mode\n#      0600 so the unprivileged service user CANNOT read it (systemd loads it as\n#      root before dropping privileges):\n#        sudo install -d /etc/routekit-eval\n#        sudo install -m 0600 -o root -g root /dev/null /etc/routekit-eval/env\n#        # then edit /etc/routekit-eval/env:\n#        #   ROUTEKIT_EVAL_BEARER_TOKEN=sk-or-...\n#        #   ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT=7070\n#   3. Install routekit-eval AS the service user into its home so it stays writable for\n#      `--auto-update` (a root-owned /usr/local/bin is unwritable by User=routekit-eval and\n#      read-only under ProtectSystem= below). This writes routekit-eval + routekit-eval.version to\n#      /var/lib/routekit-eval/.local/bin:\n#        sudo -u routekit-eval HOME=/var/lib/routekit-eval bash -lc \\\n#          'curl -fsSL --proto \"=https\" the RouteKit installation | bash'\n#   4. Materialize the gitignored SDK cache (.routekit-eval/sdk) + install deps as the service\n#      user, so the first boot can resolve the `file:.routekit-eval/sdk` dependency:\n#        sudo -u routekit-eval HOME=/var/lib/routekit-eval bash -lc 'cd /var/lib/routekit-eval && ~/.local/bin/routekit-eval init .'\n#   5. sudo cp deploy/routekit-eval.service /etc/systemd/system/\n#      sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now routekit-eval\n#\n# Full runbook: `routekit-eval start --help`\n\n[Unit]\nDescription=RouteKitEval\nDocumentation=https://routekit.dev/eval\nAfter=network-online.target\nWants=network-online.target\n\n[Service]\nType=simple\nUser=routekit-eval\nGroup=routekit-eval\n\n# The workspace that contains features/ and .routekit-eval/. SQLite state and NDJSON logs\n# resolve relative to this directory, so it must match the workspace you deployed.\n# /var/lib is the FHS home for service-owned state — not /opt (add-on software) or\n# /root (ProtectHome= below hides it from the service).\nWorkingDirectory=/var/lib/routekit-eval\n\n# Pin HOME to the workspace. The harness runtime and skill caches resolve under\n# $HOME/.routekit-eval (~/.routekit-eval/pi-runtime, ~/.routekit-eval/skills-cache), so HOME must be a writable\n# path that ProtectHome= does not hide. /var/lib is safe; a stray /home/routekit-eval would\n# be blocked by ProtectHome=true below and break skill/harness setup.\nEnvironment=HOME=/var/lib/routekit-eval\n\n# Default port so ExecStart still resolves when the env file omits ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT. Set\n# here (rather than a shell-style ${ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT:-7070} in ExecStart, which needs\n# systemd >= 249) so it works on older systemd too; the env file below overrides it.\nEnvironment=ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT=7070\n\n# Secrets + tuning. Required: ROUTEKIT_EVAL_BEARER_TOKEN (or a workspace .routekit-eval/start.json).\n# ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT is optional and defaults to 7070 above. Keep this file root-owned and\n# mode 0600: systemd reads it as root while preparing the unit, then drops to\n# User=routekit-eval, so the service process itself never reads the file. InaccessiblePaths=\n# below also hides it from the process namespace as defense in depth.\nEnvironmentFile=/etc/routekit-eval/env\n\n# Bind to loopback by default; front it with a reverse proxy for external access.\n# --global-auth lets the ROUTEKIT_EVAL_BEARER_TOKEN from the env file satisfy the\n# credential gate (or drop it and ship a workspace .routekit-eval/start.json instead).\n#\n# To auto-update in place, append `--auto-update patch --auto-update-restart exit`.\n# `exit` (not the default `reexec`) makes routekit-eval exit cleanly after swapping the binary\n# so Restart=always relaunches it from the updated /var/lib/routekit-eval/.local/bin; reexec\n# would race the systemd-managed restart and double-bind the port. Auto-update needs\n# curl + bash on the host and egress to the release host.\nExecStart=/var/lib/routekit-eval/.local/bin/routekit-eval start --global-auth --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${ROUTEKIT_EVAL_PORT}\n\nRestart=always\nRestartSec=2\n\n# --- Resource backstop ---\n# Cap the service cgroup so a leaked subprocess tree or main-process leak\n# self-limits (OOM-kill and a clean Restart=) instead of dragging the whole host\n# into swap thrash. The memory caps are percentages of the host's RAM so the same\n# unit works on any VM tier. systemd cannot substitute these from the env file, so\n# tune them per host with a drop-in (`sudo systemctl edit routekit-eval`) instead of editing\n# this file:\n#   [Service]\n#   MemoryMax=4G\n#   TasksMax=256\nMemoryHigh=53%\nMemoryMax=66%\n# Disable swap so a memory leak gets promptly OOM-killed and restarted instead\n# of silently swap-thrashing until it starves the event loop.\nMemorySwapMax=0\nTasksMax=512\n\n# routekit-eval shuts the session down cleanly on SIGTERM. KillMode=mixed sends SIGTERM to\n# the main process first, then SIGKILL to any stragglers.\nKillSignal=SIGTERM\nKillMode=mixed\n# Headroom for the runtime to tear the session scope down before systemd\n# escalates to SIGKILL.\nTimeoutStopSec=45\n\n# Treat a clean shutdown as success across restarts. `routekit-eval` exits 130 on SIGINT and\n# 143 on SIGTERM after tearing the session down, so both count as clean.\nSuccessExitStatus=0 130 143\n\n# --- Hardening (relax if your features need broader access) ---\nNoNewPrivileges=true\nPrivateTmp=true\nProtectSystem=full\nProtectHome=true\nProtectControlGroups=true\nProtectKernelTunables=true\nRestrictSUIDSGID=true\n# The workspace .routekit-eval/ must stay writable: SQLite state, NDJSON logs, and — because\n# HOME is pinned here — the harness runtime (.routekit-eval/pi-runtime), the skills cache\n# (.routekit-eval/skills-cache), and the remote-features cache (.routekit-eval/remote-features) all\n# land under it. .local/bin holds the CLI so `--auto-update` can swap the binary.\n# Both sit under /var (already writable under ProtectSystem=full); listing them\n# keeps the intent explicit and survives a tighten to ProtectSystem=strict.\nReadWritePaths=/var/lib/routekit-eval/.routekit-eval /var/lib/routekit-eval/.local/bin\n# Hide the secret env file from the running service. systemd loads it as root\n# before this sandbox applies, so the variables are still injected; the process\n# just cannot read the file back (e.g. a compromised feature cannot exfiltrate it).\nInaccessiblePaths=-/etc/routekit-eval/env\n\n[Install]\nWantedBy=multi-user.target\n"
  }
}
